1. exact absolute file:line
2. short code snippet
3. what the customer sees vs what is true
4. smallest fix

Return findings as text in your final message. Be precise with line numbers.

367	 * Inserted BEFORE `location / {` on purpose: nginx serves the first matching
368	 * regex location, so a deny rule appended after the generic `location ~ \.php$`
369	 * block would never fire for a .php URI — the wp-content/uploads shell block
370	 * would have been decorative. Throws if the shared template changes shape
371	 * rather than silently emitting an unhardened vhost.

373	function hardenVhost(vhost: string, rules: string): string {
374	  if (!rules) return vhost;

385	/**
386	 * A one-click install writes a vhost with `cat >` and extracts an archive into
387	 * the docroot. If the customer already has a hand-rolled site on this domain,
388	 * or files in that directory, doing so destroys their work — so we refuse
389	 * instead. Same for the database: the old code used CREATE DATABASE IF NOT
390	 * EXISTS / CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS, which silently adopted an existing user
391	 * WITHOUT applying the new password, leaving the customer holding credentials
392	 * that do not work.
393	 */
394	async function assertNothingToOverwrite(
395	  conn: Client,
396	  domain: string,
397	  docRoot: string,
398	  database: { engine: string; name: string; dbUser: string } | null
399	): Promise<void> {
400	  assertDomain(domain);
401	  assertPath(docRoot);
402	
403	  const conf = `/etc/nginx/sites-available/${domain}.conf`;
404	  const vhost = await exec(conn, `test -e ${shellQuote(conf)} && echo yes || echo no`, QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
405	  assert(
406	    vhost.stdout.trim() !== "yes",
407	    `An nginx site for ${domain} already exists on this server. Remove it first — the installer will not overwrite it.`
408	  );
409	
410	  const files = await exec(
411	    conn,
412	    `if [ -d ${shellQuote(docRoot)} ]; then find ${shellQuote(docRoot)} -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print 2>/dev/null | head -1; fi`,
413	    QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS
414	  );
415	  assert(
416	    files.stdout.trim() === "",
417	    `${docRoot} already contains files. Move or remove them first — the installer will not overwrite them.`
418	  );
419	
420	  if (!database) return;
421	  assertIdent(database.name, "database name");
422	  assertIdent(database.dbUser, "database user");
423	  // The whole pre-flight has to run BEFORE we change anything, which is before
424	  // ensureMysql/ensurePostgres has had a chance to install an engine. On a fresh
425	  // VM there is no client to ask — and nothing that could be overwritten — so
426	  // "engine absent" is a pass, not the hard failure an unguarded query would be.
427	  const client = database.engine === "mysql" ? "mysql" : "psql";
428	  const haveClient = await exec(
429	    conn,
430	    `command -v ${shellQuote(client)} >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo yes || echo no`,
431	    QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS
432	  );
433	  if (haveClient.stdout.trim() !== "yes") return;
434	  if (database.engine === "mysql") {
435	    const r = await execInput(
436	      conn,
437	      "mysql --protocol=socket -uroot -N -B",
438	      `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.schemata WHERE schema_name = '${database.name}';\n` +
439	        `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mysql.user WHERE user = '${database.dbUser}';\n`,
440	      SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS
441	    );
442	    if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(`could not query MySQL: ${why(r)}`);
443	    const [dbCount, userCount] = r.stdout.trim().split(/\s+/);
444	    assert(dbCount === "0", `A database named ${database.name} already exists — refusing to reuse it.`);
445	    assert(userCount === "0", `A MySQL user named ${database.dbUser} already exists — refusing to reuse it.`);
446	  } else if (database.engine === "postgres") {
447	    const r = await execInput(
448	      conn,
449	      "sudo -u postgres psql -t -A -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1",
450	      `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_database WHERE datname = '${database.name}';\n` +
451	        `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = '${database.dbUser}';\n`,
452	      SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS
453	    );
454	    if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(`could not query PostgreSQL: ${why(r)}`);
455	    const [dbCount, userCount] = r.stdout.trim().split(/\s+/);
456	    assert(dbCount === "0", `A database named ${database.name} already exists — refusing to reuse it.`);
457	    assert(userCount === "0", `A PostgreSQL role named ${database.dbUser} already exists — refusing to reuse it.`);
458	  }
459	}

465	/**
466	 * Create the app's database + user with the generated password (STDIN only),
467	 * then PROVE that credential works by connecting with it. The customer is shown
468	 * this password once and types it into the app's setup wizard; "the CREATE
469	 * statement exited 0" is not evidence that it will log in.
470	 */
471	async function provisionDb(
472	  conn: Client,
473	  engine: string,
474	  name: string,
475	  user: string,
476	  password: string
477	): Promise<void> {
478	  assertIdent(name, "database name");
479	  assertIdent(user, "database user");
480	  assertInertSecret(password, "database password");
481	
482	  if (engine === "mysql") {
483	    // No IF NOT EXISTS: assertNothingToOverwrite has already established that
484	    // neither exists, so a collision here is a real error and must surface.
485	    const sql =
486	      `CREATE DATABASE \`${name}\` CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;\n` +
487	      `CREATE USER '${user}'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '${password}';\n` +
488	      `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON \`${name}\`.* TO '${user}'@'localhost';\n` +
489	      `FLUSH PRIVILEGES;\n`;
490	    const r = await execInput(conn, "mysql --protocol=socket -uroot", sql, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
491	    if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(`database setup failed: ${why(r)}`);
492	
493	    // Log in AS the customer's user. The password reaches mysql through a 0600
494	    // defaults file written by the same shell that deletes it — never argv.
495	    const check = await execInput(
496	      conn,
497	      `umask 077; f=$(mktemp) && cat > "$f" && ` +
498	        `mysql --defaults-extra-file="$f" --protocol=socket -N -B -e 'SELECT 1' ${shellQuote(name)} >/dev/null 2>&1; ` +
499	        `rc=$?; rm -f "$f"; exit $rc`,
500	      `[client]\nuser=${user}\npassword=${password}\n`,
501	      SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS
502	    );
503	    if (check.code !== 0)
504	      throw new Error(
505	        `the generated database credentials did not work when tested — not handing the customer a password that does not log in.`
506	      );
507	  } else if (engine === "postgres") {
508	    const sql = `CREATE ROLE "${user}" LOGIN PASSWORD '${password}';\nCREATE DATABASE "${name}" OWNER "${user}";\n`;
509	    const r = await execInput(conn, "sudo -u postgres psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1", sql, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
510	    if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(`database setup failed: ${why(r)}`);
511	    // No login test: nothing in the catalogue provisions PostgreSQL, so rather
512	    // than ship an untested probe we leave the gap visible here.
513	  } else {
514	    throw new Error(`Unsupported database engine: ${engine}`);
515	  }
516	}

542	/**
543	 * Download the application and unpack it into the docroot, then verify the
544	 * payload really is that application. Returns the URL that worked.
545	 *
546	 * Everything interpolated is a fixed string from RECIPES (URLs, archive layout)
547	 * or an allowlisted path; nothing here comes from the customer.
548	 */
549	async function stageAppFiles(conn: Client, recipe: Recipe, docRoot: string, appName: string): Promise<string> {
550	  assertPath(docRoot);
551	  assert(/^[a-z0-9._-]*$/.test(recipe.top), `Unsupported archive layout: ${recipe.top}`);
552	  assert(/^[a-z0-9._/-]+$/.test(recipe.marker), `Unsupported payload marker: ${recipe.marker}`);
553	  if (recipe.archive === "zip") await ensureUnzip(conn);
554	
555	  const top = recipe.top ? `${recipe.top}/` : "";
556	  const extract = recipe.archive === "zip" ? `unzip -q "$a" -d "$t/x"` : `tar -xzf "$a" -C "$t/x"`;
557	  const urls = recipe.sources.map(shellQuote).join(" ");
558	  const dest = shellQuote(docRoot);
559	
560	  const r = await exec(
561	    conn,
562	    `set -e; t=$(mktemp -d); a="$t/pkg"; mkdir -p "$t/x"; ok=""; ` +
563	      `for u in ${urls}; do if curl -fsSL --max-time 600 -o "$a" "$u"; then ok="$u"; break; fi; done; ` +
564	      `if [ -z "$ok" ]; then rm -rf "$t"; echo "NXAPP:NODOWNLOAD" >&2; exit 20; fi; ` +
565	      `if ! ${extract}; then rm -rf "$t"; echo "NXAPP:BADARCHIVE" >&2; exit 21; fi; ` +
566	      `if [ ! -e "$t/x/${top}${recipe.marker}" ]; then rm -rf "$t"; echo "NXAPP:BADPAYLOAD" >&2; exit 22; fi; ` +
567	      `mkdir -p ${dest}; cp -a "$t/x/${top}." ${dest}/; rm -rf "$t"; ` +
568	      `printf 'NXAPP:FROM %s\\n' "$ok"`,
569	    INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS
570	  );
571	  const out = `${r.stdout}\n${r.stderr}`;
572	  if (/NXAPP:NODOWNLOAD/.test(out))
573	    throw new Error(`could not download ${appName} from any known release URL — nothing was changed on the server.`);
574	  if (/NXAPP:BADARCHIVE/.test(out)) throw new Error(`the ${appName} download was not a readable archive.`);
575	  if (/NXAPP:BADPAYLOAD/.test(out))
576	    throw new Error(`the ${appName} download did not contain ${recipe.marker} — refusing to treat it as ${appName}.`);
577	  const from = /NXAPP:FROM (\S+)/.exec(r.stdout);
578	  if (r.code !== 0 || !from) throw new Error(`${appName} download failed: ${why(r)}`);
579	
580	  // Prove the files landed where nginx will look, rather than trusting cp -a.
581	  const marker = await exec(
582	    conn,
583	    `test -e ${shellQuote(`${docRoot}/${recipe.marker}`)} && echo yes || echo no`,
584	    QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS
585	  );
586	  assert(marker.stdout.trim() === "yes", `${appName} files are missing from ${docRoot} after unpacking.`);
587	  return from[1];
588	}

613	/**
614	 * Write wp-config.php and run WordPress's real installer so the admin account
615	 * the customer was shown actually exists.
616	 *
617	 * Two things the old version got wrong and this must not:
618	 *  - it defined ONE weak AUTH_KEY, so every site shared guessable cookie salts;
619	 *    all eight keys are now 48 random bytes each.
620	 *  - it never ran an installer, so the "admin password shown only once" opened
621	 *    nothing. We call wp_install() and then re-read the user and check the
622	 *    password against the stored hash before anyone is told it works.
623	 *
624	 * The script is written to a 0600 file OUTSIDE the docroot (never web-reachable)
625	 * by the same shell invocation that runs and deletes it, and carries the admin
626	 * password in its body — via STDIN, never argv.
627	 */
628	async function installWordpress(
629	  conn: Client,
630	  domain: string,
631	  docRoot: string,
632	  phpVersion: string,
633	  creds: { name: string; user: string; password: string },
634	  admin: { user: string; password: string; email: string }
635	): Promise<void> {
636	  assertDomain(domain);
637	  assertPath(docRoot);
638	  assertPhp(phpVersion);
639	  assertIdent(creds.name, "database name");
640	  assertIdent(creds.user, "database user");
641	  assertIdent(admin.user, "admin user");
642	  assertInertSecret(creds.password, "database password");
643	  assertInertSecret(admin.password, "admin password");
644	
645	  const salts = WP_SALT_KEYS.map((k) => `define('${k}', '${rand()}');`).join("\n");
646	  const cfg =
647	    `<?php\n` +
648	    `/* Generated by the Nxeon control panel — one-click WordPress install. */\n` +
649	    `define('DB_NAME', '${creds.name}');\n` +
650	    `define('DB_USER', '${creds.user}');\n` +
651	    `define('DB_PASSWORD', '${creds.password}');\n` +
652	    `define('DB_HOST', 'localhost');\n` +
653	    `define('DB_CHARSET', 'utf8mb4');\n` +
654	    `define('DB_COLLATE', '');\n` +
655	    `${salts}\n` +
656	    `define('WP_DEBUG', false);\n` +
657	    // Deliberately NOT defining WP_HOME/WP_SITEURL: hardcoding http:// here
658	    // would grey out Settings → General and strand the customer on http after
659	    // they enable SSL from this panel. The installer seeds the URL options
660	    // instead, so WordPress can be moved to https from its own admin.
661	    `$table_prefix = 'wp_';\n` +
662	    `if ( ! defined('ABSPATH') ) define('ABSPATH', __DIR__ . '/');\n` +
663	    `require_once ABSPATH . 'wp-settings.php';\n`;
664	  const wrote = await execInput(
665	    conn,
666	    `umask 037; cat > ${shellQuote(`${docRoot}/wp-config.php`)}`,
667	    cfg,
668	    SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS
669	  );
670	  if (wrote.code !== 0) throw new Error(`could not write wp-config.php: ${why(wrote)}`);
671	
672	  const script =
673	    `<?php\n` +
674	    `/* Nxeon one-click WordPress finish — run once, then deleted. */\n` +
675	    `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'] = ${php(domain)};\n` +
676	    `$_SERVER['SERVER_NAME'] = ${php(domain)};\n` +
677	    `$_SERVER['SERVER_PORT'] = '80';\n` +
678	    `$_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] = '/';\n` +
679	    `$_SERVER['SCRIPT_NAME'] = '/index.php';\n` +
680	    `$_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] = 'GET';\n` +
681	    // wp_guess_url() honours WP_SITEURL, so the siteurl/home options are seeded
682	    // with the real domain instead of a CLI-derived guess.
683	    `define('WP_SITEURL', ${php(`http://${domain}`)});\n` +
684	    `define('WP_HOME', ${php(`http://${domain}`)});\n` +
685	    `define('WP_INSTALLING', true);\n` +
686	    `require_once ${php(`${docRoot}/wp-load.php`)};\n` +
687	    `require_once ABSPATH . 'wp-admin/includes/upgrade.php';\n` +
688	    `if ( is_blog_installed() ) { fwrite(STDERR, "NXWP:ALREADY\\n"); exit(31); }\n` +
689	    `$res = wp_install(${php(domain)}, ${php(admin.user)}, ${php(admin.email)}, true, '', ${php(admin.password)});\n` +
690	    `if ( is_wp_error($res) ) { fwrite(STDERR, 'NXWP:ERR ' . $res->get_error_message() . "\\n"); exit(32); }\n` +
691	    `$uid = ( is_array($res) && isset($res['user_id']) ) ? $res['user_id'] : 0;\n` +
692	    `if ( is_wp_error($uid) || (int) $uid < 1 ) { fwrite(STDERR, "NXWP:NOUSER\\n"); exit(33); }\n` +
693	    `$u = get_user_by('login', ${php(admin.user)});\n` +
694	    `if ( ! $u || (int) $u->ID !== (int) $uid ) { fwrite(STDERR, "NXWP:NOACCOUNT\\n"); exit(34); }\n` +
695	    // The whole point: prove the password we are about to show authenticates.
696	    `if ( ! wp_check_password(${php(admin.password)}, $u->user_pass, $u->ID) ) { fwrite(STDERR, "NXWP:BADPASS\\n"); exit(35); }\n` +
697	    `if ( ! in_array('administrator', (array) $u->roles, true) ) { fwrite(STDERR, "NXWP:NOTADMIN\\n"); exit(36); }\n` +
698	    `echo "NXWP:OK user=" . (int) $u->ID . "\\n";\n`;
699	
700	  const run = await execInput(
701	    conn,
702	    `umask 077; f=$(mktemp) && cat > "$f" && ` +
703	      `p=$(command -v php${phpVersion} 2>/dev/null || command -v php 2>/dev/null); ` +
704	      `if [ -z "$p" ]; then rm -f "$f"; echo "NXWP:NOPHP" >&2; exit 30; fi; ` +
705	      `"$p" "$f"; rc=$?; rm -f "$f"; exit $rc`,
706	    script,
707	    INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS
708	  );
709	  const out = `${run.stdout}\n${run.stderr}`;
710	  // WordPress's own wp_die() prints its message and exits 0, so a zero exit
711	  // code proves nothing here — the OK marker is the only accepted evidence.
712	  if (/NXWP:OK/.test(run.stdout)) return;
713	  if (/NXWP:NOPHP/.test(out)) throw new Error("no PHP CLI binary on the server — cannot complete the WordPress install.");
714	  if (/NXWP:ALREADY/.test(out)) throw new Error("this database already contains a WordPress install — refusing to overwrite it.");
715	  if (/NXWP:BADPASS|NXWP:NOACCOUNT|NXWP:NOUSER/.test(out))
716	    throw new Error("WordPress ran but the admin account could not be verified — not reporting an install we cannot prove.");
717	  if (/Error establishing a database connection/i.test(out))
718	    throw new Error("WordPress could not connect to its database with the generated credentials.");
719	  throw new Error(`WordPress setup failed: ${why(run)}`);

724	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

726	/**
727	 * Fetch one path on the app's own domain FROM INSIDE the VM, with the hostname
728	 * pinned to 127.0.0.1 (`curl --resolve`). That sends the real Host header, so it
729	 * genuinely tests "does this vhost serve this application" while remaining
730	 * correct before the customer's DNS has propagated. Mirrors the probe in
731	 * worker/migrate-real.ts, which exists because a port check proved only that
732	 * something was listening while sites returned 502s.
733	 */
734	async function httpProbe(conn: Client, domain: string, path: string): Promise<{ code: string; body: string }> {
735	  assertDomain(domain);
736	  assert(/^\/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]*$/.test(path), `Unsupported probe path: ${path}`);
737	  const r = await exec(
738	    conn,
739	    `f=$(mktemp); c=$(curl -sS -k -L --max-redirs 5 --max-time 25 ` +
740	      `--resolve ${shellQuote(`${domain}:80:127.0.0.1`)} --resolve ${shellQuote(`${domain}:443:127.0.0.1`)} ` +
741	      `-o "$f" -w '%{http_code}' ${shellQuote(`http://${domain}${path}`)} 2>/dev/null); ` +
742	      `[ -n "$c" ] || c=000; printf 'NXCODE:%s\\n' "$c"; head -c 8192 "$f" 2>/dev/null; rm -f "$f"`,
743	    SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS
744	  );
745	  const out = String(r.stdout ?? "");
746	  const m = /NXCODE:(\d{3})/.exec(out);
747	  const nl = out.indexOf("\n");
748	  // Keep newlines: stripping them would glue words together and make markers
749	  // unmatchable (see probeBody in worker/migrate-real.ts).
750	  // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
751	  const body = (nl < 0 ? "" : out.slice(nl + 1)).replace(/[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]/g, " ");
752	  return { code: m ? m[1] : "000", body };
753	}

755	/**
756	 * Run every probe for the app. Throws with the real HTTP result on the first
757	 * failure — an install that cannot be proved is a FAILED install, never a
758	 * quietly-downgraded one. Returns a one-line proof for the audit trail.
759	 */
760	async function verifyServing(conn: Client, domain: string, probes: Probe[]): Promise<string> {
761	  const proof: string[] = [];
762	  for (const p of probes) {
763	    const { code, body } = await httpProbe(conn, domain, p.path);
764	    if (!(p.codes ?? ["200"]).includes(code))
765	      throw new Error(`verification failed: ${p.path} returned HTTP ${code}, so ${p.proves} is not true.`);
766	    for (const re of p.reject ?? []) {
767	      const hit = re.exec(body);
768	      if (hit) throw new Error(`verification failed: ${p.path} returned an application error ("${hit[0].slice(0, 80)}").`);
769	    }
770	    for (const re of p.require) {
771	      if (!re.test(body))
772	        throw new Error(`verification failed: ${p.path} answered 200 but ${p.proves} could not be confirmed.`);
773	    }
774	    proof.push(`${p.path}=${code}`);
775	  }
776	  return `verified from the VM (${proof.join(" ")})`;
777	}

783	export async function appInstall(job: Job): Promise<void> {
784	  const app = await loadApp(job);
785	  const catalog = appBySlug(app.appSlug);
786	  const info = appMode(app.appSlug);
787	  await db.appInstall.update({ where: { id: app.id }, data: { status: "INSTALLING" } });
788	
789	  try {
790	    assertSlug(app.appSlug);
791	    assertDomain(app.domain);
792	    assert(catalog, `Unknown app: ${app.appSlug}`);
793	    // A queued job from before this app was withdrawn must not be able to
794	    // produce an ACTIVE row for an install nobody can perform.
795	    assert(info.mode !== "unavailable", `${catalog!.name} is not available as a one-click install. ${info.remaining}`);
796	    const recipe = RECIPES[app.appSlug];
797	    assert(recipe, `No installer recipe for ${app.appSlug}.`);
798	
799	    const website = app.websiteId ? await db.website.findUnique({ where: { id: app.websiteId } }) : null;
800	    const database = app.databaseId ? await db.vpsDatabase.findUnique({ where: { id: app.databaseId } }) : null;
801	    const docRoot = website?.docRoot ?? `/var/www/${app.domain}`;
802	    const url = `http://${app.domain}/`;
803	    assertPath(docRoot);
804	
805	    // Nextcloud's wizard defaults its data directory to <docroot>/data, which the
806	    // vhost would then happily serve. Give the customer a path outside the
807	    // docroot to paste in (and keep the deny rules as a second line of defence).
808	    const dataDir = `/var/lib/nxeon-apps/${app.domain}/data`;
809	    const detailParts: string[] = [];
810	
811	    if (info.mode === "assisted") {
812	      detailParts.push(`${catalog!.name} files are in ${docRoot}.`);
813	      if (database) detailParts.push(`Database ${database.name} (user ${database.dbUser}) on localhost is ready.`);
814	      if (app.appSlug === "nextcloud")
815	        detailParts.push(
816	          `Use ${dataDir} as the data folder — it sits outside the web root, so nothing can be downloaded ` +
817	            `straight off the URL, and "Remove" here will not delete your files.`
818	        );
819	      detailParts.push(info.remaining);
820	    }
821	
822	    const status: "ACTIVE" | "NEEDS_SETUP" = info.mode === "managed" ? "ACTIVE" : "NEEDS_SETUP";
823	    let detail = detailParts.join(" ");
824	
825	    if (REAL) {
826	      const dbPass = database ? decryptSecret(database.passwordEnc) : null;
827	      const adminPass = decryptSecret(app.adminPassEnc);
828	      if (database) assert(dbPass, "The generated database password could not be decrypted.");
829	      if (info.mode === "managed") {
830	        assert(app.adminUser && adminPass, "The generated admin password could not be decrypted.");
831	        assert(catalog!.php, `${catalog!.name} needs a PHP version in the catalogue.`);
832	      }
833	      const owner = await db.user.findUnique({ where: { id: app.userId }, select: { email: true } });
834	      const adminEmail =
835	        owner?.email && /^[^\s@]{1,64}@[A-Za-z0-9.-]{1,190}$/.test(owner.email) ? owner.email : `admin@${app.domain}`;
836	
837	      const server = await sshServer(app.serverId);
838	      const proof = await withServerSsh(server, async (conn) => {
839	        // 0. Nothing of the customer's gets overwritten. Runs before any change.
840	        await assertNothingToOverwrite(conn, app.domain, docRoot, database);
841	
842	        // 1. Runtime + site (vhost + docroot), with app-specific hardening.
843	        await ensureNginx(conn);
844	        if (catalog!.php) {
845	          await ensurePhpFpm(conn, catalog!.php);
846	          await ensurePhpExtensions(conn, catalog!.php, recipe.phpExt);
847	        }
848	        await exec(conn, `mkdir -p ${shellQuote(docRoot)}`, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
849	        const conf = `/etc/nginx/sites-available/${app.domain}.conf`;
850	        const link = `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/${app.domain}.conf`;
851	        await execInput(
852	          conn,
853	          `cat > ${shellQuote(conf)}`,
854	          hardenVhost(nginxVhost(app.domain, docRoot, catalog!.php), recipe.nginx),
855	          SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS
856	        );
857	        await exec(conn, `ln -sf ${shellQuote(conf)} ${shellQuote(link)}`, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
858	
859	        // 2. Database — created, then proved to accept the generated password.
860	        if (database && dbPass) {
861	          if (database.engine === "mysql") await ensureMysql(conn);
862	          else if (database.engine === "postgres") await ensurePostgres(conn);
863	          await provisionDb(conn, database.engine, database.name, database.dbUser, dbPass);
864	        }
865	
866	        // 3. The application's REAL files (never a placeholder page).
867	        const from = await stageAppFiles(conn, recipe, docRoot, catalog!.name);
868	
869	        // 4. Managed apps only: complete first-run setup. Asserted rather than
870	        // skipped-if-missing — a silently skipped installer is how "ACTIVE with
871	        // a placeholder" happened in the first place.
872	        if (info.mode === "managed") {
873	          assert(app.appSlug === "wordpress", `No managed installer exists for ${app.appSlug}.`);
874	          assert(database && dbPass, `${catalog!.name} cannot be installed without its database.`);
875	          await installWordpress(
876	            conn,
877	            app.domain,
878	            docRoot,
879	            catalog!.php!,
880	            { name: database.name, user: database.dbUser, password: dbPass },
881	            { user: app.adminUser!, password: adminPass!, email: adminEmail }
882	          );
883	        }
884	        if (app.appSlug === "nextcloud") {
885	          assertPath(dataDir);
886	          await exec(
887	            conn,
888	            `mkdir -p ${shellQuote(dataDir)} && (chown -R www-data:www-data ${shellQuote(dataDir)} 2>/dev/null || ` +
889	              `chown -R nginx:nginx ${shellQuote(dataDir)}) && chmod 750 ${shellQuote(dataDir)}`,
890	            SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS
891	          );
892	        }
893	
894	        // 5. Ownership/permissions, then serve.
895	        await applyOwnership(conn, docRoot);
896	        await reloadNginx(conn);
897	
898	        // 6. VERIFY. Until this returns, nothing is reported to the customer.
899	        const verified = await verifyServing(conn, app.domain, recipe.probes);
900	        return `${verified}; files from ${from}`;
901	      });
902	      detail = info.mode === "managed" ? proof : `${detail} (${proof})`;
903	    } else {
904	      // Sandbox/simulated: say so, and still honour the app's declared mode so
905	      // staging never shows a greener outcome than production would produce.
906	      detail = `${detail} Sandbox: no VM was touched.`.trim();
907	    }
908	
909	    if (website) await db.website.update({ where: { id: website.id }, data: { status: "ACTIVE", ssl: false, error: null } });
910	    if (database) await db.vpsDatabase.update({ where: { id: database.id }, data: { status: "ACTIVE", error: null, passwordEnc: null } });
911	    await db.appInstall.update({
912	      where: { id: app.id },
913	      // `error` is the row's status-detail line (the schema has no note column);
914	      // the panel renders it amber for NEEDS_SETUP, never as a failure.
915	      data: { status, url, error: detail.slice(0, 900) || null, adminPassEnc: null },
916	    });
917	
918	    const href = `/dashboard/servers/${app.serverId}?tab=control panel`;
919	    if (status === "ACTIVE") {
920	      const signIn = app.appSlug === "wordpress" ? `${url}wp-login.php` : url;
921	      await notify(
922	        app.userId,
923	        `${catalog!.name} is installed and serving on ${app.domain}`,
924	        REAL
925	          ? `Sign in at ${signIn} with the admin user and password shown at install — the account exists and that ` +
926	            `password was checked against it before this message was sent. ${detail}`
927	          : `${catalog!.name} installed (sandbox — no real VM was touched). URL: ${url}`,
928	        href
929	      );
930	    } else {
931	      await notify(
932	        app.userId,
933	        `${catalog!.name} on ${app.domain} is ready for you to finish setup`,
934	        `Nxeon prepared the site, the database and ${catalog!.name}'s files, but the install is NOT complete — ` +
935	          `${catalog!.name} creates its own admin account in its setup wizard. ${detail}`,
936	        href
937	      );
938	    }
939	  } catch (e: any) {
940	    const reason = String(e?.message ?? e).slice(0, 400);
941	    // Never keep secrets on a failed install.
942	    if (app.databaseId) await db.vpsDatabase.update({ where: { id: app.databaseId }, data: { status: "FAILED", error: reason, passwordEnc: null } }).catch(() => {});
943	    if (app.websiteId) await db.website.update({ where: { id: app.websiteId }, data: { status: "FAILED", error: reason } }).catch(() => {});
944	    await db.appInstall.update({ where: { id: app.id }, data: { status: "FAILED", error: reason, adminPassEnc: null } });
945	    await notify(app.userId, `${catalog?.name ?? "App"} install failed on ${app.domain}`, reason.slice(0, 200), `/dashboard/servers/${app.serverId}`);
946	  }
947	}

Looking at some critical issues in the codebase: the websiteCreate function in worker/websites.ts is marking sites as ACTIVE without actually performing any HTTP verification, which is a significant gap. Then there's the shell command chain for directory setup and permissions — the `|| true` at the end masks failures from both the mkdir and chown operations, so even if the directory creation fails, the script still exits successfully and the execution result goes unchecked.

The bigger problem is in reloadNginx at line 131 — it runs `systemctl reload nginx || systemctl restart nginx` but never checks the return code, so if both commands fail, the function still reports success and marks the site as ACTIVE. This is especially dangerous for websites since there's no downstream verification like there is for apps. The websiteToggle function has a similar issue where it sets ACTIVE after just a symlink and reload without any actual verification. The websiteSsl function does at least check certbot's output for success markers, though that's only a partial gate since it's based on output patterns rather than actual certificate validation. The rm command doesn't verify success either, so if deletion fails the database row gets removed anyway but the vhost stays live and keeps serving — that's a false success claim worth flagging as medium severity. In databases.ts, dbCreate marks the database ACTIVE and ready without actually testing a connection with the generated credentials, unlike the apps provisioning which does verify login. MySQL's password alteration works, but there's no proof it connects; Postgres has error checking but also skips the connection test.

Looking at ensureMysql, the systemctl enable command result isn't checked, though downstream failures would catch it when the mysql client command runs. There's a subtle issue though: `command -v mysql` only checks for the client binary, not whether the server is actually running, so if the client exists but the server doesn't, ensureMysql returns early thinking everything's fine.

In dbDelete, the execInput call that removes the database isn't validated, so the database could be deleted from the application's perspective while still existing on disk with data intact. And in serviceAction, checking systemctl's exit code isn't fully reliable—a service can start successfully according to systemctl but then crash immediately after, or restart and fail in ways that still return 0. The cronSync function marks all cron rows as ACTIVE regardless of whether they're disabled, and while it does install the crontab and check the exit code, it doesn't verify the actual contents were written. There's also a risk that if `crontab -l` fails for reasons other than having no crontab (like command not found), the base variable stays empty and we proceed with incomplete data. The UI probably handles the enabled toggle separately, which is a minor issue. In claude.ts, the executePhase function marks status as DONE after commands complete based on SSH exit codes, then sends a notification claiming the build succeeded — but there's no verification that the app actually serves. The real problem is that commands blocked by the denylist are silently skipped, yet the final status still shows DONE, so a build where a critical command was blocked falsely reports success.

The sshExec function treats stderr as acceptable and only fails on non-zero exit codes, which means commands like `apt-get install -y foo || true` generated by Claude can mask failures. If sshpass isn't installed, it throws ENOENT and fails properly. The server validation checks for ipAddress and password before proceeding, which is fine. There's also something about terminal builds at line 169 that's cut off.

Now looking at the sandbox branch — there's a real inconsistency here. The code sets a DONE status and sends a notification saying "Claude finished building on <hostname>" without any indication it's a sandbox simulation, even though the log contains "[sandbox] simulated build completed". This is different from websites.ts which explicitly labels things as "(sandbox — no real VM was touched)". So customers get a notification claiming a build finished on their server when nothing actually ran. That's worth flagging.

Moving into apps.ts now to check the verified path for serving — the verifyServing function does a real HTTP probe with a mark.

Checking the verification chain: installWordpress uses wp_check_password for password verification, provisionDb runs a mysql login test, stageAppFiles has a marker check. For applyOwnership, the chown is checked but the find/chmod result isn't validated on lines 602-606 — though a permissions failure would likely surface in the HTTP probe anyway, so it's minor. ensurePhpExtensions doesn't check the systemctl restart result on line 539, but again the probes would catch it.

Looking at the mkdir and symlink operations: mkdir -p for docRoot isn't checked, but stageAppFiles has its own mkdir -p later so that's fine. The ln -sf for the config link on line 857 isn't checked either, but the probe would catch any failure there too. For the website status updates around line 909, both managed and assisted apps set the Website row to ACTIVE after the probe passes, which is accurate since the website is genuinely serving. The sandbox branch also sets status to ACTIVE for managed apps when not in REAL mode, with the detail noting "Sandbox:" The error swallowing in the catch block at lines 939-946 is actually safe since it fails loudly on the appInstall update rather than claiming success. There's a minor issue where the website row stays in its previous state if the DB update fails, but that's not critical. In the REAL branch, decryptSecret gets called with null for assisted mode adminPassEnc, which just returns null — that's fine. I've read every file in scope plus the call sites that consume them. Here are the findings.

---

# VERIFICATION-GATE AUDIT — one-click apps, Build with AI, websites, databases, claude-code

**Key semantic that makes most of these bugs real:** `exec()` / `execInput()` in `/opt/nxeon/lib/ssh-exec.ts:115-176` **resolve** with `{code, stdout, stderr}` — a non-zero exit does **not** throw. Every `await exec(...)` whose return value is discarded is a silent-failure site.

---

## VERIFIED OK — do NOT re-report these as bugs

`worker/apps.ts` is genuinely fixed. It is the reference implementation for the rest of the platform.

| What | file:line | Why it counts as a real gate |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP probe from inside the VM, Host pinned via `curl --resolve` | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:734-753` | Real GET, real Host header, works pre-DNS |
| `verifyServing()` — status code + required body markers + reject markers, **throws** on first failure | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:760-777` | An unprovable install FAILS; never downgraded to "needs setup" |
| The gate is placed before any customer-facing write | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:898-901` (`// 6. VERIFY. Until this returns, nothing is reported`) | Status/URL/notification all happen after |
| WordPress probes include `/wp-admin/install.php` requiring "already installed" and rejecting the setup form | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:216-228` | Proves `wp_install()` really ran, not just that PHP served something |
| Admin password proved against the stored hash before it is shown as working | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:696` (`wp_check_password(...)` → `NXWP:BADPASS`) + role check `:697` | This is the P1-22 fix; correct |
| Exit code explicitly rejected as proof; only the `NXWP:OK` marker accepted | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:709-719` | Comment + code agree |
| DB credentials proved by logging in **as the customer's user** via a 0600 defaults file | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:495-506` | "the generated database credentials did not work when tested" |
| Download payload verified (`NXAPP:BADPAYLOAD`) **and** re-verified in the docroot after `cp -a` | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:566` and `:581-586` | curl exit 0 is not trusted |
| Pre-flight refuses to overwrite an existing vhost / non-empty docroot / existing DB or user | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:394-459` | Also fixes the `IF NOT EXISTS` silent-adopt bug |
| `chown` failure is now fatal (the old `\|\| true` is gone) | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:600-601` | Explicitly called out in the comment |
| Withdrawn app can't be resurrected by a stale queued job | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:795` | `assert(info.mode !== "unavailable", ...)` |
| Assisted apps settle to `NEEDS_SETUP`, never ACTIVE — including in sandbox | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:822`, `:903-907` | Staging can't look greener than prod |
| `hardenVhost` throws instead of silently emitting an unhardened vhost | `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:373-379` | |
| Panel refuses unavailable apps up front; no admin password minted for assisted apps; honest install note | `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-apps.ts:181`, `:241`, `:266-270` | The promise matches the installer |
| `NEEDS_SETUP` renders amber, never the green ACTIVE pill | `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/cpanel/shared.tsx:26-28` | |
| Claude build: plan-then-approve; nothing runs before owner approval | `/opt/nxeon/worker/claude.ts:223-227`; `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-claude.ts:118-123` | |
| Claude build: per-command exit code checked, execution **stops** on first failure | `/opt/nxeon/worker/claude.ts:322-326` | |
| `reloadNginx` runs `nginx -t` and throws on a bad config | `/opt/nxeon/worker/websites.ts:129-130` | Partial — see F4 for the un-checked reload itself |
| `websiteSsl` requires exit 0 **and** a certbot success marker in the output | `/opt/nxeon/worker/websites.ts:219-221` | Partial — see F6; no HTTPS fetch, but far better than the old invented-expiry code |

---

## FINDINGS

### F1 — CRITICAL: Websites marked `ACTIVE` + "is live" + "serving" with zero HTTP verification, and every shell step unchecked
`/opt/nxeon/worker/websites.ts:150-171`

```ts
150  await exec(conn, `mkdir -p ${shellQuote(site.docRoot)} && chown -R www-data:www-data ${shellQuote(site.docRoot)} 2>/dev/null || true`, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
151  await execInput(conn, `cat > ${shellQuote(site.docRoot + "/index.html")}`, `...Your Nxeon-hosted site is live.`, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
158  await execInput(conn, `cat > ${shellQuote(conf)}`, nginxVhost(...), SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
160  await exec(conn, `ln -sf ${shellQuote(conf)} ${shellQuote(link)}`, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
162  await reloadNginx(conn);
...
165  await db.website.update({ where: { id: site.id }, data: { status: "ACTIVE", error: null } });
169  REAL ? "Your nginx site is configured and serving." : ...
```

Not one of lines 150/151/158/160 checks `.code`. Line 150's `|| true` covers the whole `mkdir && chown` chain, so a failed `mkdir` exits 0. If the docroot can't be created, `cat >` fails silently, the vhost write fails silently, and the symlink fails silently — and the row still becomes `ACTIVE`.

**Customer sees:** green "ACTIVE" pill and a clickable `http://domain` link (`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/cpanel/WebsitesPanel.tsx:205,230`), plus a notification titled "Website *domain* is live" saying "Your nginx site is configured and serving."
**Truth:** ACTIVE means "the job ran without an exception". Nothing ever fetched the site. A 502/404/stock-nginx page is indistinguishable from a working one. This is the exact defect class `worker/apps.ts` was rewritten to eliminate — apps proves it, websites does not.

**Smallest fix:** lift `httpProbe`/`verifyServing` out of `worker/apps.ts:734-777` into a shared module (`lib/ssh-exec.ts` or `lib/http-probe.ts` — `apps.ts` already imports *from* `websites.ts`, so a direct import would be circular), then after line 162:
```ts
await verifyServing(conn, site.domain, [{ path: "/", require: [/Nxeon-hosted site is live/i], proves: "the domain serves this site" }]);
```
and check `.code !== 0` on 150/151/158/160.

---

### F2 — CRITICAL: `ACTIVE` is the *precondition* for SSL, so F1 propagates
`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-websites.ts:282`

```ts
if (site.status !== "ACTIVE") return { ok: false, error: "The website must be active before enabling SSL." };
```

**Customer sees:** the "Enable SSL" button offered (`WebsitesPanel.tsx:261` gates on `status === "ACTIVE"`) because the row says ACTIVE.
**Truth:** the site may not serve at all, so certbot's HTTP-01 challenge cannot succeed — the customer gets a confusing certbot failure for a site the panel told them was live.
**Smallest fix:** fixing F1 fixes this; no change needed here.

---

### F3 — HIGH: Databases marked `ACTIVE` and "is ready" without ever connecting with the generated password
`/opt/nxeon/worker/databases.ts:111-130`

```ts
111  const r = await execInput(conn, "mysql --protocol=socket -uroot", sql, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
112  if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(`MySQL create failed: ...`);
...
126  await db.vpsDatabase.update({ where: { id: row.id }, data: { status: "ACTIVE", error: null, passwordEnc: null } });
129  REAL ? `Your ${row.engine} database and user are provisioned.` : ...
```

Compare `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:495-506`, which does exactly the missing check and comments *"the CREATE statement exited 0 is not evidence that it will log in."* The standalone DB creator never got that fix.

Aggravating detail on line 107-108: `CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS ... ; ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED BY '<pass>'` — the `IF NOT EXISTS` silently adopts a pre-existing user (the ALTER does re-apply the password, but any pre-existing grants/host rows are inherited unexamined). `apps.ts:483-485` explicitly refuses to do this.

**Customer sees:** green ACTIVE pill, "Database *name* is ready", and a password shown **once** (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-databases.ts:162`) that they will paste into an app.
**Truth:** the password is proved only by root's DDL exiting 0. `passwordEnc` is then nulled at line 126, so if the credential doesn't work there is no recovery — the customer holds a password nobody can re-derive.

**Smallest fix:** before line 126, run the same login probe as `apps.ts:495-506` (MySQL: 0600 `--defaults-extra-file` + `SELECT 1 <db>`; Postgres: `PGPASSWORD` via a file/env with `psql -c 'SELECT 1'`). Throw on failure so the row goes FAILED **while `passwordEnc` still exists**, or delay the null until the probe passes.

---

### F4 — HIGH: `reloadNginx` reports success even when nginx is down
`/opt/nxeon/worker/websites.ts:128-132`

```ts
129  const test = await exec(conn, "nginx -t", SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
130  if (test.code !== 0) throw new Error(`nginx config test failed: ...`);
131  await exec(conn, "systemctl reload nginx || systemctl restart nginx", SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);   // result discarded
```

The config test is checked; the actual reload/restart is not. If nginx is masked, out of memory, or the port is taken, both commands fail and this function returns normally.

**Customer sees:** website ACTIVE / app ACTIVE.
**Truth:** for apps, `verifyServing()` catches it (that path is safe). For **websites** it is unguarded — this is F1's most likely real-world trigger.
**Smallest fix:**
```ts
const r = await exec(conn, "systemctl reload nginx || systemctl restart nginx", SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(`nginx reload failed: ${(r.stderr || r.stdout).trim().slice(0,200)}`);
const up = await exec(conn, "systemctl is-active nginx", QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
if (up.stdout.trim() !== "active") throw new Error("nginx is not active after reload");
```

---

### F5 — HIGH: "Build with AI" reports DONE when the load-bearing command was silently skipped
`/opt/nxeon/worker/claude.ts:311-314`, `:305`, `:333`, `:339-342`

```ts
311  // Defense-in-depth: even an approved plan is re-checked against the denylist.
312  if (isForbidden(command)) {
313    await append(`\n$ ${command}\n[nxeon] Skipped — blocked by the safety denylist.\n`, steps);
314    continue;                       // <-- no effect on finalStatus
   ...
305  let finalStatus: "DONE" | "FAILED" = "DONE";
333  await db.claudeBuild.update({ where: { id: buildId }, data: { status: finalStatus, steps } });
340  finalStatus === "DONE" ? `Claude finished building on ${server.hostname}` : ...
```

A plan whose only meaningful step trips the denylist (`passwd`, `systemctl restart …ssh…`, anything matching `\bdd\b[^|]*of=/dev/`) skips that step, executes nothing else of consequence, and finishes as **DONE**.

**Customer sees:** emerald "DONE" pill (`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/ClaudeBuilder.tsx:131`) and a notification "Claude finished building on *host*".
**Truth:** the requested work was never done. More broadly, DONE means "every non-skipped command exited 0" — there is no probe that the built thing serves, despite `lib/ai-build.ts` prompts that all end in *"Then run it and tell me the URL to preview it."*

**Smallest fix (skipped steps):** track skips and force the outcome:
```ts
let skipped = 0;
if (isForbidden(command)) { skipped++; ...; continue; }
...
if (skipped > 0 && finalStatus === "DONE") finalStatus = "FAILED";   // or a distinct PARTIAL status
```
**Larger fix (serving):** after execution, if the plan mentions a port/service, run `systemctl is-active <unit>` or `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` and append the result to the log before settling the status.

---

### F6 — HIGH: `claude-code` "pre-installed on every server" is asserted to every customer; the install is `|| true` and never verified
`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:113-114`

```ts
113  "npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code || true",
114  "command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'Claude Code installed' >> /var/log/nxeon-setup.log || true",
```

Line 113 swallows every failure (no npm, no network, EACCES, registry 5xx). Line 114 *looks* like a verification gate but (a) also ends in `|| true`, (b) writes to a log file nothing in this repo ever reads (grep confirms `/var/log/nxeon-setup.log` has no reader), and (c) has no effect on any status or DB row.

Worse, the claim is emitted **before the install can even start**: cloud-init `write_files` (lines 165-178) runs before `runcmd` (183-186), and the installer is backgrounded with `nohup` (line 186). So the MOTD is already on disk claiming the tool exists:

- `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:153` — `"Nxeon — Claude Code is pre-installed on this server."` (MOTD, every login)
- `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:129` — `"## Build anything with Claude Code — it's already installed"` (`~/START-WITH-CLAUDE.md`)
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx:277` — `"Claude Code is pre-installed on every Nxeon server."`
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx:288` — green **"Already installed"** badge, rendered unconditionally
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx:341` — terminal mock: `"Welcome to your Nxeon server — Claude Code is pre-installed."`
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/ai-build.ts:70` — `"Claude Code is already installed on your VPS."`
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/ai-build.ts:97` and `:160` — `"Welcome to Nxeon VPS - Claude Code is pre-installed"`

**Customer sees:** an unconditional platform guarantee, in the portal, in the MOTD and in a file in their home directory.
**Truth:** nothing anywhere records whether `claude` exists on that box. A customer whose npm install failed types `claude`, gets `command not found`, and the banner right above it says it's pre-installed.

**Smallest fix:** persist the result and let the UI read it. Have the setup script write a machine-readable sentinel (`command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 && touch /var/lib/nxeon/claude-ok`), probe it once over SSH when the server first reports RUNNING, store `Server.claudeCodeReady: boolean`, then gate `ClaudeCodeHub.tsx:277/288/341` on it ("Claude Code is installed on this server" vs. "Setting up — run `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` if it isn't there yet"). At minimum drop `|| true` from line 113 so the install failure is visible in the setup log.

---

### F7 — MEDIUM: Docker add-on: "preinstalled" claim, no verification
`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:118`

```ts
118  if (addons.docker) setup.push("curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && systemctl enable --now docker");
```
vs. `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:395`:

```ts
{ k: "docker", t: "Docker manager", tag: "Free", d: "Docker + Compose preinstalled to deploy containers instantly." }
```

**Customer sees:** "Docker + Compose preinstalled to deploy containers instantly" on a card they select at checkout.
**Truth:** if `get.docker.com` is unreachable or the distro is unsupported, the VM boots with no docker and nothing notices.
**Smallest fix:** append `docker ps >/dev/null 2>&1 && touch /var/lib/nxeon/docker-ok` to the same chain and surface it the same way as F6.

### F8 — MEDIUM: Website delete reports success even when nothing was removed from the server
`/opt/nxeon/worker/websites.ts:248-257`

```ts
248  await exec(conn, `rm -f ${shellQuote(link)} ${shellQuote(conf)}`, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);   // unchecked
251  if (site.docRoot.startsWith("/var/www/")) {
252    await exec(conn, `rm -rf ${shellQuote(site.docRoot)}`, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);            // unchecked
254  await reloadNginx(conn).catch(() => {});                                              // swallowed

```

**Customer sees:** the site vanishes from the panel.
**Truth:** the vhost may still be enabled and serving their content to the internet, and the docroot may still be on disk consuming quota — with no row left to retry from. The `.catch(() => {})` on 254 additionally hides a broken nginx config caused by the removal.
**Smallest fix:** check `.code` on 248/252 and re-probe: `test -e <conf> -o -e <link> && echo left || echo gone`; only `db.website.delete` when it reports `gone`, otherwise leave the row in `DELETING` with an error.

### F9 — MEDIUM: Database delete has the identical hole
`/opt/nxeon/worker/databases.ts:155`, `:160`, `:164`

```ts
155  await execInput(conn, "mysql --protocol=socket -uroot", sql, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);   // unchecked
160  await execInput(conn, "sudo -u postgres psql", sql, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);            // unchecked, and no ON_ERROR_STOP=1
```

**Customer sees:** database removed.

### F10 — MEDIUM: Sandbox Claude build notifies "Claude finished building on your server" with no sandbox disclaimer
`/opt/nxeon/worker/claude.ts:181-199`

```ts
186  status: "DONE",
187  log: truncate((build.log ?? "") + "\n[sandbox] simulated build completed\n", MAX_LOG_CHARS),

193  title: `Claude finished building on ${server?.hostname ?? "your server"}`,
194  body: build.prompt.slice(0, 140),
```

Every other worker in this codebase says so explicitly — `/opt/nxeon/worker/websites.ts:169` (`"(sandbox — no real VM was touched)"`), `/opt/nxeon/worker/databases.ts:130`, `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:927`, `/opt/nxeon/worker/services.ts:161`. This one doesn't: the disclaimer is buried in the build log, and the notification body is just the customer's own prompt.

**Customer sees:** "Claude finished building on *hostname*".
**Truth:** nothing ran, no SSH, no Anthropic call.
**Smallest fix:** append the same parenthetical to the notification body: `body: \`${build.prompt.slice(0,140)} (sandbox — no real VM was touched)\``.

### F11 — LOW/MEDIUM: `cronSync` marks every row `ACTIVE`, including disabled ones, and never reads the crontab back
`/opt/nxeon/worker/services.ts:105-114`

```ts
105  const cur = await exec(conn, "crontab -l 2>/dev/null || true", QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
106  const base = stripManaged(cur.stdout);
   ...
110  const r = await execInput(conn, "crontab -", body, SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS);
111  if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(...);
```

1. Line 114 has no `enabled` filter — a **disabled** cron row, which is deliberately absent from the installed crontab, is written `ACTIVE`.
2. Line 105's `|| true` means any non-"no crontab" failure of `crontab -l` (missing binary, transient permission error) yields empty stdout, so line 107 installs a crontab containing only the Nxeon block — **silently wiping the customer's hand-written cron entries**, then reporting ACTIVE.

**Customer sees:** all cron rows green.
**Truth:** disabled jobs claim ACTIVE; in the failure case their own crontab was destroyed and the panel says everything is fine.

### F12 — LOW: `serviceAction` notifies "Started/Restarted *unit*" without an `is-active` check, and may act on the wrong php-fpm unit
